facts.title: The Mechitharist Fathers
facts.text: An Armenian Catholic order guided by a maxim: “neither sacrifice nation to religion, nor religion to nation.”

facts.title: Founded in Constantinople
facts.text: Mekhitar of Sebaste founded his order there. Persecuted, the monks moved to Modon, in the Morea, then under Venetian control.

facts.title: The island of San Lazzaro
facts.text: Seeking refuge in Venice, the congregation received the perpetual concession of the island from the Senate of the Republic.

facts.title: The first dictionary
facts.text: Mekhitar published the Bargirk Haykazian Lezui, the first comprehensive dictionary of the Armenian language.

facts.title: Lord Byron at San Lazzaro
facts.text: Byron visited the island, and Father Pascal Aucher became his Armenian tutor.

facts.title: Venice and Vienna reunited
facts.text: Divided in 1773, the two branches reunified: San Lazzaro became the headquarters again, Vienna the primary abbey.

facts.title: 4,000 years
facts.text: Nearly that old: an Egyptian mummy, kept with its sarcophagus among ancient manuscripts and early printed Bibles.

ytTitle: The Mechitharist Fathers of Venice and Vienna, three centuries of Armenian letters
ytLead: Founded in 1701 by Mekhitar of Sebaste, the Mechitharist Fathers turned the island of San Lazzaro in Venice, and later Vienna, into centers of the Armenian language and letters.
